prose.text: The block runs: phase A (formatter, linter, the three crates' units, the viola-mcp suite, the call-deadline control's filtered entry, the error-bodies census, the tokio and rmcp gates); phase B (the rig library cases, the `MB` rehearsals through the integration layer, which builds the root binaries they spawn); the round (entries 14–26, `round` and `live` entries ONLY, `inputs#I2` item 10), its after-reads of state other actors move keyed to the round; after the span the census keyed `operator` and the report-only ledger read; then the whole layers and the operator pass. What is not run, and why: no mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 10); no release-check entry (CI's `release` job runs it); `cargo deny check` is CI's `supply-chain` job (no dependency is added, a feature only; the tokio bans are entries 8–9). Every test start runs under a test-owned home; every waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s lint, the handlers' held reply a 5 s backstop. The live starts run under the rig's private scratch and config; the rig's `--deadline` bounds each under its entry's `timeout`. The non-priming probes of each live leg are the round entries ahead of it. The whole-round dry-run is shown on the P5 card.
**The remove-the-guard control** is implement's one-shot `gate.py control`, never an entry:

| | `call-deadline` | |---|---| | **File** | `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` | | **The edit removes** | the deadline over `frame()`: the frame awaited alone, the seam's future never polled | | **Case** | `handlers_frame_tools_end_at_the_call_deadline::case_1_send` | | **Fired on** | entry 6, `--timeout 300` |

With the guard removed the call returns the canned reply at the wrapper's 5 s backstop, the case reads its detail red, and no `TIMEOUT` line can stand for it (300 s against a 5 s backstop); a `timeout` reading would NOT read the guard as held. The filter selects 0 tests on the untouched tree and the four cases once they exist.

**The live atoms' must-pass readings** (validation check 4 (9)): the `MB` summary keys the three live entries assert are this chunk's own print site (step 10), so each word is read printed before any graded use, in block order: entry 10 runs the reader's cases of step 9, which produce every word the atoms name (`call-error: false`/`true`, `timed-out: true`, `cut-word: tool-timeout`, `elapsed-band: at-cap`/`at-bound`) from synthetic lines; entry 11 runs the arm's rehearsal of step 12, which prints the arm's own keys (`arm: mb`, `keys: none`, `wrapped: ready`, `mcp-timeout: none`/`5000`, `client: exit 0`) and the rig's teardown keys over the fake agent. A live atom that only a real client can print (`call-error`, `timed-out`, `cut-word`, `elapsed-band` read from real stream-json) is the reading itself (`inputs#I2` item 5 names the predicate).
